summary.intent: Implement and ship a large batch of CipherBox v2 issues (#618, #624, #623, #645, then #619/#631/#646/#637) using parallel worktree/background agents, run security and code review passes, and merge PRs via the /ship loop.
summary.outcome: Shipped and merged #618 (PR #659), #623/#645/#624 (rebased and merged as #662/#660/#661), and shipped #619/#637/#646/#631 (PRs #664, #663 merged, #666, #668) with review findings fixed; discovered and fixed a branch-protection deadlock from the desktop-build matrix and a CI startup-failure from an unallowlisted GitHub Action; coordinated CodeRabbit's 1-review/hour org quota across simultaneous PRs.

repo: GitHub Actions org policy uses a `selected` allowlist; an unlisted action causes silent `startup_failure` with zero jobs even though actionlint/zizmor pass — check repo Actions permissions when a workflow appears 'stuck'.

Registering matrix-leg check contexts (e.g. `Desktop Build (macos-latest)`) as required status checks deadlocks any PR whose path filter skips that matrix (contexts never report) — must add an always-reporting `if: always()` gate job (`needs: <matrix-job>`) and require that single stable context instead.
Registering a new required status check before any PR reports it (or before merge) can permanently block sibling PRs — always register post-merge, once the context is proven on a real run.

CodeRabbit enforces an org-wide 1-web-review-per-hour cap; it auto-reviews on PR-ready and does NOT auto-resume after a rate-limit drop — manual `@coderabbitai review` retrigger is only appropriate after CodeRabbit itself posts a quota-depleted comment.
crates/core det-CBOR: major-7 dispatch must key off the additional-info (ai) field, not the raw arg, or half-float bit patterns alias simple values (e.g. `f90014` decodes as `false`).
reqwest 0.13's rustls feature forces aws-lc-rs (needs cmake/nasm); use reqwest 0.12 with `rustls-tls-webpki-roots` (ring backend) to avoid the toolchain dependency in CI/dev.
Linux `sync-secret-service` keyring crate pulls in libdbus (C), violating a pure-Rust constraint; use `async-secret-service`/zbus/async-io instead.

kat_gen (crates/core/examples/kat_gen.rs) must be the sole writer of manifest.json — preserving header fields from the existing file on disk lets hand-edits survive the CI freshness diff; hardcode the header in the generator instead.

CI freshness checks for generated KAT vectors must also fail on untracked files under the kat directory, not just modified ones (`git status --porcelain`), or a new vector file could be silently omitted.

code.finding: Display impl for writer-controlled map keys needed a DISPLAY_KEY_MAX_CHARS=64 cap (DisplayKey wrapper) to bound plaintext volume in error messages/logs, found by crypto-privacy-review.

write_value needed a debug_assert!(depth < MAX_DEPTH) guard plus a caller-obligation doc comment on encode(), since the encoder is otherwise infallible and could produce undecodable output for pathologically deep Values.
blinded_tag_bytes/pseudonym_sign_bytes built the HKDF `ikm` from secret material in a plain Vec that dropped unwiped; needed explicit ikm.zeroize() before return (CodeRabbit Major finding).
extract_and_expand moved the DHKEM shared secret out of a bare Vec via try_into, freeing the buffer unwiped; wrapped in Zeroizing (CodeRabbit Minor finding).

desktop-build job is a path-filtered matrix; needs an always-reporting desktop-build-result gate job (needs: desktop-build, if: always()) so a single stable required context exists regardless of whether the matrix ran or was skipped.

workflow: Orchestrating many parallel worktree agents (implement + ship loops) works well but needs active supervision: agents repeatedly 'stall' after reporting a genuine wait (CI/CodeRabbit/reviews) because their own background monitor doesn't keep them alive — must poll PR state directly and SendMessage a nudge ('continue to completion, do not stop between steps') to resume them.

After a base branch is squash-merged, stacked/rebased sibling branches need Cargo.lock (or lockfile) regeneration during rebase conflict resolution — this recurred across #631, #646, #637, #619, #664, #666.
Merge order matters when multiple PRs touch the same Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock or ci.yml region — the second-merged always needs a trivial rebase; plan and communicate this upfront.

Two-axis review pattern (Standards + Spec agents in parallel) plus a dedicated crypto-privacy-review skill catches real issues (zeroization gaps, path traversal, timing leaks) beyond what CI/tests catch.
When user gives a durable process correction (e.g. CodeRabbit quota staggering), capture it to memory immediately so it persists across future sessions instead of being re-learned.

friction: GitHub Actions appeared 'stuck' but was actually silently startup_failure due to an unallowlisted action — not visible via actionlint/zizmor, only discoverable via check-run annotations and Actions permissions API.
PR #668 desktop build checks appeared 'stuck' but were actually a branch-protection deadlock (required contexts that a TS-only PR's path filter would never report).
CodeRabbit's 1-review/hour org quota collided with running 4 ship loops simultaneously, causing premature/wasted manual review requests until the user corrected the approach.
Ship agents repeatedly parked/stalled mid-loop after legitimate waits (CI, CodeRabbit, review threads) without a live background child, requiring manual SendMessage nudges to resume them.

CodeRabbit's rate-limit reset time reported in its own PR comment was itself inaccurate/misleading once (11:42Z request got only an incremental 'already reviewed' ack, not a real review; true reset was ~11:56Z per user correction).
Committing the crypto-privacy-review security report to .planning/security/ violated the user's no-commit-reports preference, requiring a history rewrite (reset --hard + force-with-lease) to remove.
open_items: Issue #665 filed: harden StagingStore unlink-ordering durability on Windows (fsync_dir is a no-op there; low severity since Windows isn't a current target).
Issue #667 filed: mailbox 90-day TTL is lazy-only (no scheduled sweep), so dormant mailboxes can retain expired rows indefinitely.
PR #666 (desktop seams) needs its post-#663 rebase completed and its CodeRabbit review requested in the next available quota window (~12:56Z queue slot).

PR #669 (desktop-build-result gate) has one open Greptile thread (pass needs.desktop-build.result via env: instead of direct ${{ }} interpolation) — fix was in progress (actionlint + commit) when transcript ends.

After #664/#666/#668/#669 all merge, need to register the new required checks (API Unit/Migration Drift/OpenAPI Freshness were already done; Desktop Build Result gate still pending registration) and handle final lockfile/ci.yml rebases.
